I can't give you a confirmed list. I couldn't run a cycle detector, so this comes from reading the imports by hand.

I tried madge and a small script, but there's no `node_modules` and the script run needed approval. Instead I grepped the imports in `packages/core/injector` and checked which ones are used as values. TypeScript drops imports that are only used as types, so those don't count as runtime edges.

**Within `injector/` itself, I found no runtime cycle.** The files import each other mostly as types, which the compiler drops. For example, `module.ts` takes `NestContainer` only as a type, and `instance-wrapper.ts` takes `Module` only as a type. `constants.ts` takes `ContextId` as a type. The real value edges (`new`, `extends`, `.name`, constants) run one way:

- `container` → `module`, `modules-container`, `internal-core-module`
- `module` → `module-ref`, `instance-wrapper`
- `module-ref` → `abstract-instance-resolver`, `injector`, `instance-links-host`, `instance-wrapper`
- `injector` → `instance-wrapper`, `settlement-signal`, `constants`

None of these lead back to `container`.

**A cycle through other directories is still possible, and I couldn't rule it out.** The edge to check is `container.ts` → `inspector/serialized-graph.ts`, a real value import (`new SerializedGraph()`). `serialized-graph.ts` imports these as values:
- `module-ref`
- `lazy-module-loader`
- `modules-container`
- `helpers/external-context-creator`
- `services/reflector.service`

For a cycle, one of those would have to import `container` at runtime. `lazy-module-loader`, `module-ref` and `modules-container` don't. I didn't trace `external-context-creator` and its dependencies (guards, pipes, router), or `errors/exceptions`, far enough to say.

To get a definitive answer, run `npx madge --circular --extensions ts packages/core/injector` or `npx dpdm --transform packages/core/injector/index.ts`. Both need an install. If you approve me running a short Node script that does the same graph analysis, I can do it here.

I found no runtime import cycle among the files in `packages/core/injector`. I couldn't confirm that with a tool: the dependency-checker script I wrote was blocked, and `madge` and `typescript` aren't installed here. This comes from reading the imports and usages by hand, so I haven't run a tool over it.

**Why the cycle-looking imports aren't runtime cycles**

The imports look cyclic, but most of the back-edges are only used as types. With no `verbatimModuleSyntax` and no decorators on these classes, TypeScript drops those imports when it compiles.

- **`constants.ts` → `instance-wrapper.ts`:** `ContextId` is used only as a type annotation.
- **`instance-wrapper.ts` → `module.ts`:** `Module` is used only as a type, for `host?: Module`.
- **`injector.ts` → `module.ts`:** `Module` appears only in parameter types and `Set<Module>`.
- **`module.ts` → `container.ts`:** `NestContainer` is used only as a constructor parameter type.
- **`module-ref.ts` → `container.ts`, `module.ts`:** both are used only as types.
- **`abstract-instance-resolver.ts` → `injector.ts`, `module.ts`, `instance-links-host.ts`:** all are used only as types. Its `errors/exceptions` import is a value import, but that points outside `injector/`.
- **`instance-links-host.ts` → `container.ts`, `instance-wrapper.ts`, `module.ts`:** all are used only as types. Its import of `errors/exceptions/unknown-element.exception` is a value import, but it's outside `injector/`.
- **`lazy-module-loader.ts` and `internal-core-module-factory.ts` → `scanner.ts`:** `DependenciesScanner` is used only as a constructor parameter type. These classes aren't decorated, so no decorator metadata keeps the import alive.

**What remains at runtime**

The value-level imports form a one-way graph:

- `container` → `module`, `modules-container`, `compiler`, `internal-core-module`, `internal-providers-storage`
- `module` → `module-ref`, `instance-wrapper`, `constants`
- `module-ref` → `injector`, `abstract-instance-resolver`, `instance-links-host`, `instance-wrapper`, `constants`
- `injector` → `instance-wrapper`, `constants`, `settlement-signal`, `inquirer`
- `instance-wrapper` → `constants`, `helpers/provider-classifier`
- `scanner` (outside `injector/`) → `internal-core-module-factory`, which leads on to `injector`, `instance-loader` and `lazy-module-loader`

Nothing in that set leads back to a file already on its path.

**Caveats**

- I didn't read the multi-line import blocks in full. I also only partly checked the files in `core/` that import from `injector/` (`errors`, `discovery`, `helpers`, `inspector`, `application-config`).
- If you need certainty, run `npx madge --circular --extensions ts packages/core/injector`. Madge counts type-only imports as edges unless you pass a tsconfig and `--ts-config`, so it may report cycles that disappear at runtime. I can run it, or the script, if you approve the command.

**None of the files in `packages/core/injector` take part in a runtime import cycle.** That comes from reading the code by hand. I couldn't run `madge` or any other tool, because the command needed approval that wasn't granted.

For each import I checked whether it is used as a value (`new`, `extends`, passed as a token) or only as a type, since TypeScript drops type-only imports from the compiled output. I checked every pair of files that imports each other:

| Apparent cycle | Why it isn't a runtime cycle |
|---|---|
| `module.ts` ↔ `module-ref.ts` | `module.ts` extends and uses `ModuleRef` as a value. `module-ref.ts` uses `Module` only as a parameter type (`module-ref.ts:163`). |
| `module.ts` ↔ `container.ts` | `container.ts` calls `new Module` as a value. `module.ts` uses `NestContainer` only as a constructor parameter type (`module.ts:73`). |
| `constants.ts` ↔ `instance-wrapper.ts` | `constants.ts` uses `ContextId` only as a type annotation (`constants.ts:6`). |
| `instance-wrapper.ts` → `module.ts` | The only use is the type `host?: Module` (`instance-wrapper.ts:65`). |
| `injector.ts`, `abstract-instance-resolver.ts`, `instance-links-host.ts`, `modules-container.ts` → `module.ts` / `container.ts` | All of these uses are type annotations. |
| `abstract-instance-resolver.ts` → `injector.ts`, `instance-links-host.ts` | Both are used only as abstract property types, so the imports are dropped. |

I also checked for cycles that leave the folder and come back, and found none:

- **`container.ts` → `inspector/serialized-graph` → `lazy-module-loader` → `module-ref`:** this chain never returns to `container.ts`. `module-ref` imports `NestContainer` only as a type.
- **`internal-core-module-factory.ts` → `scanner.ts` → `internal-core-module-factory.ts`:** this looks like a loop, but the factory uses `DependenciesScanner` only as a parameter type. The `scanner` → factory edge is one-way at runtime.
- **`errors/exceptions/*` → `injector/injector`, `injector/module`:** type-only imports.
- **`helpers/*` → `injector/constants`, `injector/instance-wrapper`:** these point inward and nothing points back. `helpers/external-context-creator` uses `NestContainer` and `ModulesContainer` only as types.

I didn't open every file outside the folder that `internal-core-module` pulls in (for example `services/reflector.service.ts`). The few I did check had no imports pointing back into the injector.
